 Order

The complainants have filed the writ petition in W.P.No.202022/2023 for directions to the Deputy Commissioner, Kalaburagi, and the Assistant Commissioner/Special Land Acquisition Officer,
Sedam, to send a reference to the competent Court under Section 30 of the Land Acquisition Act,
1894, as per the order dated 27.09.1982.

The complainant have asserted that the land measuring 19 acres in Sy.No.322 of Diggaon village, Chittapur Taluk, Kalaburagi District is notified for acquisition under the Karnataka Industrial Area Development Act and that though there is recommendation for reference, appropriate reference order is not passed.

The writ Court, in the light these assertions,
has issued a writ of mandamus which reads as under:
 i. The writ petition is allowed.
 ii.

A mandamus is issued, directing respondents  No.3 and 4 to implement the order dated 27.09.1982 at Annexure-B by forwarding the file to the appropriate Jurisdictional Court within a period of thirty days from the date of receipt the copy of this order.
This Court must observe that the Special Land Acquisition Officer, Karnataka Industrial Area Development Board and the Land Officer Sedam/ the Assistant Commissioner of Sedam Sub- NC: 2024:KHC-K:1547-DB Division, after some interse communication, which are rather is reconcilable, are ultimately able to place on record copy of the reference Order dated 11/13.10.1982 and the culmination in this order reads as under:
"The counsel for Sri.Siddappa s/o Shivyogappa contended that Sri.Siddappa is the owner and possessor of Sy. No.322 of Diggaon Village and he has not sold the land to Sri.Vithoba and that all the revenue records stand in the name of Sri.Siddappa and before the Land Tribunal Chitapur

entities.text: Special Land Acquisition Officer, Karnataka Industrial Area Development Board
entities.label: PETITIONER

sentences.text: , Sri.Vithoba has taken a stand to state that he is a tenant of the said sy. No. and now he is taking the stand of the owner before the Land Acquisition Officer to receive the compensation.

Further it was argued that the land sy. No.322 to the extent of 19 acres 22 guntas has been purchased for Rs.400/- only,
so the sale deed is fabricated and bogus and the compensation awarded may be paid to Sri. Siddappa.
After hearing the arguments of both the counsels, it is under stood that there is a dispute-of-ownership and it is out of the jurisdiction of this Court.
This dispute of ownership can be decided by the Civil Court.
Hence as required U/Sec. 30 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894(Central Act of 1894), I am referring this case to the Civil Judge, Gulbarga for deciding the dispute of ownership.

sentences.text: If there is an order for reference as aforesaid way back in the year 1982, the question of compliance with the directions in the writ Court will not arise and hence the contempt proceedings must be closed.

However, Sri.Sanjeevkumar C.Patil, the learned counsel for the complainant submits that this Court must observe, in the NC: 2024:KHC-K:1547-DB interest of justice, that the complainants would be at liberty to make application for release of the amount in deposit consequent to a decree in their favour in O.S.No.294/1989, which he says has culminated in favour of the complainants with the disposal of RSA.No.2227/2005 on 18.03.2016.

It would suffice for this Court to observe,
while closing the contempt proceedings, that if indeed the complainants can establish a decree in their favour as against those claims that are resulted in reference as aforesaid, the complainants must be at liberty in law subject to all just exceptions.
Hence, the complaint stands disposed of.
